_what: The population growth rates g_n that the committed OG-UK run actually used, vendored so a re-run does not depend on a live UN World Population Prospects fetch.

_provenance.source: results/scenarios.json -> baseline.g_n_used, i.e. p.g_n[:5] as recorded by uk_growth_with_ai.solve.run_arm for the committed baseline
_provenance.note: OG-Core's g_n[t] is growth from t to t+1.

_limitations: Only the first 5 periods were ever recorded. OG-Core needs g_n over T+S periods, so the tail of the path the committed run used is NOT recoverable from anything in this repository. The override therefore replaces ONLY g_n[:5] on the Specifications object built by oguk.api._build_specs and leaves the tail as fetched: OG-Core lands the population path on its steady state (TPI uses p.g_n[:T-1] then p.g_n_ss; SS uses p.g_n_ss), and g_n_ss was never recorded, so holding a flat vendored tail against a live g_n_ss would put a population-growth mismatch at the terminal boundary.

g_n is only one of several objects oguk.api._build_specs takes from the same live demographic fetch. omega, omega_SS, omega_S_preTP, rho, imm_rates and g_n_ss were not recorded and are still fetched live, so the solve is NOT network-free: only the reported window's g_n is pinned, and it is not guaranteed mutually consistent with the population weights the aggregates use.

The recorded path is FLAT at about 0.77%/yr (0.771% in 2026, 0.760% in 2030). OG-UK's own vendored default in og_uk_params.json DECLINES (0.748% -> 0.625%), and the OBR's labour-supply growth declines faster still, to 0.5% by 2030 (March 2026 EFO para 1.9). docs/OG_UK_OBR_COMPARISON.md describes a declining path and is stale: it was written against the vendored default, not against what the run used. The array below is what the run used (flat). Substituting a declining path is a modelling decision, not a fix, and is left open (see .audit/07-calibration-sensitivity.md section 3).
g_n_tail: live (not vendored; only g_n[:5] is pinned)
